To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) We can automatically extract structured information from unstructured text using state-of-the art statistical models and (b) We can automatically integrate this extracted structured information into a database using a variety of constraints.

(1) the performance of the stateof-the-art models can be significantly improved by exploiting the structure of the database and (2) this improvement can be achieved without sacrificing the ability to learn the models from limited amounts of labeled data.

(i) the integration of unstructured data into databases is an important problem, which can be addressed with current statistical methods; (ii) a database of entities can significantly help the extraction of structure from text, and (iii) the integration of the extracted data into a database requires a combination of the inference algorithms of the statistical models with database constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of integrating unstructured data into an existing database.
the problem of how to integrate unstructured records into a relational database in a way that preserves the semantics of the original data and the integrity of the database.
two major issues. First, we show how to effectively integrate unstructured text into relational databases using statistical models for information extraction and matching.
